security_privacy_cost_impact: Security: a local tool only; no grant, policy, role, schema or CI change. try-it makes a cluster outside the repository that listens on 127.0.0.1 only, over TCP, with no unix socket, and trusts local connections while it is up (any process on the machine can connect as the superuser; it holds synthetic fixtures only; TRY-IT.md says so; A1 owes the call on a per-cluster password, open_blockers[196] (2)). Every URL it builds passes the repository's testHostRefusal narrowed to loopback names and a non-reserved port; it refuses 5432 and the measurement ports; `down` deletes only a directory holding its marker and nothing but what `up` made. Privacy: synthetic fixtures only, no real data. Cost: none; no dependency, no service. REVIEW ROUND: A1 F1 is MEDIUM: trust on loopback is the superuser and can run operating-system commands as the Owner while a cluster is up; TRY-IT.md's Safety section now says so and says to run `down` as soon as you are done; a per-cluster scram-sha-256 password is owed before a make/npm entry point (open_blockers[196] (2)). `down` now acts only when the marker's port passes tryItRefusal, no owned entry is a symlink, postmaster.pid names this data directory and port, and the server on that port serves this data directory (A1 F2); the repository check reads a not-yet-made path through its nearest existing ancestor (A1 F3). FIX AFTER THE RE-CHECKS (A1 R-F1): the trust described above is gone. Each cluster gets a random 32-byte password; initdb stores only its scram-sha-256 verifier; the password lives in <dir>/pgpass (0600, exclusive create) and reaches connections through PGPASSFILE (an inherited PGPASSWORD is dropped); it is never in a URL, an argument or printed output (measured by grep). A process that cannot read that file is refused (measured: no password, and a wrong one). Not covered, and TRY-IT.md says so: a program running as the Owner can read the file, and the superuser can run OS commands, so `down` promptly stays the advice. The runners now enter main() by real paths (C0-TIR-1, A1 R1).
